heros.infro: Faraj ben Sālim, also known as Ferrarius, was a Sicilian-Jewish doctor and translator who lived and worked in the thirteenth century. His primary claim to fame is the translation of major Arabic medical works into Latin, including a 1279 translation of al-Razi's famous medical encyclopedia. Charles of Anjou was so grateful for his work that he ordered that the portrait of Faraj should be drawn beside his own.
heros.name: Ferrarius

heros.infro: Queen Consort of Henry VI, she saw it as her mission to defend the interests of the crown, a lesson learned from her paternal grandmother, Yolande of Aragon, who governed that land.  Her alliances with the Earl of Suffolk and the Duke of Somerset made her unpopular, and when she failed to invite the Duke of York to a meeting of the king's closest advisors in 1455, the War of the Roses began.  After Henry was captured, she escaped with her son to Wales and Scotland, and attempted to raise an army to fight Edward IV.  Her final defeat came at the Battle of Tewksbury in 1471, where her son was killed.  Afterwards, she was taken prisoner until the French king ransomed her.
heros.name: Margaret of Anjou
